criterion: The home page opens on its photographic scene carrying the headline, so the scene is the first thing seen rather than a row of navigation chrome.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the first screen of the home page is dominated by the hero scene and its headline. Answer no when navigation, cards or a feature list occupy the first screen ahead of the scene.

criterion: Inside the signed-in product the transaction list, the payment queue and the approvals queue are dense tabular surfaces built for scanning down a column.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those three surfaces render rows in aligned columns at a compact rhythm. Answer no when any of the three renders as a marketing-style card grid or carries an oversized hero.

criterion: Colour roles are declared once at the document root as named surface, text, icon and border roles with their pointed-at and pressed variants, and components consume those roles.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the computed styles resolve component colours through root-level custom properties named by role. Answer no when a component hard-codes a colour value of its own.

criterion: One blue carries the primary action on the home page, the pricing page and the application steps, and nothing else on those pages wears that blue.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the brand blue appears only on the single primary control of each page. Answer no when a heading, a border, a badge or a secondary control also wears that blue.

criterion: One magenta carries error messages across the application steps and the studio forms, and that magenta appears on nothing in a working state.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the error colour appears only on error text, error borders and error icons. Answer no when the same magenta also decorates a heading, a chart, a badge or a link.

criterion: The developers route runs on the inverted ground using the same components the light routes use.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the developers route renders dark with the same buttons, cards and type roles seen elsewhere. Answer no when the dark route is built from a second set of components or renders light.

criterion: Every empty list in the product, from the approvals queue to the reconciliation breaks, names the content that would fill the list plus the action to take.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each empty list carries a sentence naming its content and an action, and the legal routes hold their measure to a comfortable reading width at every window size. Answer no when an empty list renders as a blank area or as a bare dash.

criterion: The cookie bar sits along the foot of the page, and the partner-bank disclosure stays readable beside that bar.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the bar is anchored at the foot and the disclosure sentence remains readable. Answer no when the bar is a centred modal or covers the disclosure.

criterion: A navigation panel opens square across its top edge and rounded along its bottom, so the panel reads as hanging from the header.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the open panel meets the header with square upper corners and softens at the bottom. Answer no when the panel is evenly rounded on all four corners or floats clear of the header.

criterion: Buttons, inputs, cards and table rows across the product share one small corner softening, and the pill shape is reserved for the navigation trigger.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those elements share one modest radius and only the navigation trigger is a pill. Answer no when several radii compete on one screen or when ordinary controls are pills.

criterion: Cards on the pricing page and panels in the product separate from their ground by a faint edge or a very soft lift rather than by a ladder of drop shadows.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when separation comes from a hairline border or a barely visible lift. Answer no when several shadow depths are used to rank surfaces.

criterion: A dark wash sits between the hero scene and the headline on the home page, so the headline and the disclosure stay legible over the brightest part of the scene.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a gradient wash darkens the scene behind the type. Answer no when the type sits directly on the scene with the brightest region behind the words.

criterion: Menus, banners, accordions and page transitions across the site share one movement speed and one easing character, and the celebration on the application decision is the single exception.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every ordinary transition feels the same length and shape and only the decision step carries the falling celebration. Answer no when several speeds compete or when the celebration runs elsewhere.

criterion: Under a reduced-motion preference the sliding logo row on the home page becomes a row the reader can scroll by hand, and the legal routes stay still.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the marquee becomes scrollable and every other movement lands on its end state. Answer no when the marquee freezes with content out of view or when movement continues.

criterion: On a window that is short rather than narrow, the home page hero gives up its full-height treatment and lets the content flow.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a short window shows the hero at natural height with its actions reachable. Answer no when the hero keeps a full-height box and squashes or clips the headline.

criterion: A colour value is written directly on a component on the pricing page instead of being taken from the root colour roles.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a computed component colour resolves to a literal value rather than a root role. Answer no when every component colour resolves through a named root role.

criterion: The grain over the illustration panels on the home page is delivered as a downloaded image file.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a raster or vector file is fetched to draw the grain. Answer no when the grain is generated in the browser from a filter.
